questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My connection to the region in terms of my education. Being able to further develop my spoken Arabic.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was difficult for me to get the needed information about the availability of the courses at AUC, which was only provided when I arrived at campus in the first week. More transparency about this proces before arrival would have been nice. Otherwise I was provided with the needed support and help from the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: In the first week on AUC I was introduced to IPSO (the international office) who was very helpful and provided with all the support and help I needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found an shared appartment on Airbnb

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If exchange students choose to live off campus it can be nice to know that they will use a lot of time on transport to and from campus. In average I used +2 hours every day on transport.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This grading is based on the process before arriving to AUC. I found it very difficult to get contact to IPSO before arrival and get informations about the avialibility of the different courses. After my arrival it was easier to get the need information and I liked the possibility of trying different courses before the final decision during the first week.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied for different courses back in May, which was based on my research about the different courses on AUC's website. Some of the course descriptions was not updated, it was unclear if they would be avaible. Overall a tricky process, which resulted in me being unknowing about which courses I could expect to get when I arrived at AUC.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: IPSO was first a help after arrival at campus in the first week.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up having completely different courses than the ones I applied for before arrival.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: That they should first expect to get updated information about the available courses when they arrive at AUC and that they can choose other courses during the first week of attendance.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was overall satisfied with the academic standard of the courses, especially my one MA-course, which provided me with many new academic perspectives. In general the BA-courses was interesting and the professors had a high academic standard compared to the level of the courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some of my BA-courses was based a lot of memorizing the material of the course, which I found disappointing, coming from an insitution where critical thinking and learning is valued and prioritized, not only memorizing.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Intermediate Arabic (ALNG 2101)
Zionism and Modern Judaism (HIST 3208)
City of Cairo (ARIC 2206) 
Mobilities: Gender & Migration (GWST 5104)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Mobilities: Gender & Migration (GWST 5104) was an amazing course and the absolute peak of my courses this semester at AUC. I was provided with new perspectives and all the material used in the course was interesting. The monthly essay's challenged me to reflect critically over the material.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The student visa suddenly raised to triple the amount of the original price, from 50 to 150 dollars.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Buying groceries and cooking myself, transport to and from AUC

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Different student clubs. I joined the al-Quds club, which is working for raising awareness of Palestine and displaced Palestinians in Egypt. We arranged different events during the semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a club if you want to meet students from different educations. Find a language partner to develop your Arabic.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Trip to Sinai, Alexandria, el-Fayyoum.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy as I just spend a semester in Jordan, so it was not my first time to live in an Arab country.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Find a language partner and join a club.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In general I found the sexual harrasment based on my gender challeging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The welcoming and friendly culture. It is very easy to make friends in Egypt

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be prepared for long transport days if you live outside campus (fx. in Downtown, Zamalek or Maadi)
- therefor try to arrange your schedule with a day or two without courses.
2. There is a heavy constant workload, which is quite different from the University of Copenhagen. Try to take it easy eventhough it can be stressful 
3. Enjoy and look forward to explore Egypt and Cairo - the city is amazing.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Always contact IPSO if there is anything you're unsure about - they can help you with anything.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
New academic reflections and perspectives. 
Living in Cairo and creating friendships and learning about the culture and the country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The suppresion of free speech. Was challenging due to the genocide in Gaza.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
